newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain could use military base as relief airport.
newsitem.headline: Spain could use military base as relief airport.

text.p: The Spanish government is considering using a former U.S. military base at Torrejon just east of Madrid to relieve overcrowding at the capital's Barajas airport, a spokesman for the air traffic authority AENA said.
Torrejon has a runway of more than four kms, sufficient to accommodate even the biggest commercial aircraft and is a only few kilometres further east of the city than Barajas, AENA said.
Its use is being seriously considered to ease delays over the next two years while a third runway at Barajas is being built, Development Minister Rafael Arias Salgado said.

A contract to build the third runway was awarded on Monday to a group of three construction companies, but it will not be completed until the beginning of 1999 and delays at Barajas have worsened to the extent that 50 percent of flights were affected last month.
Once completed the third runway will increase the number of flights Barajas can handle to an average of 85 an hour at peak times from 50 now.
